title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1RC0RA_1LA0LD_1LE0RB_1RD1LF_0LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1RC0RA_1LA0LD_1LE0RB_1RD1LF_0LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its tape is a list of counters written as runs of 01 or 10. It has two regimes. Both are proved in Lean one round trip at a time for every size. What is not proved is how the run passes from one regime to the next. This page lists what has been established, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the following by the kernel. First, the round trip of the right-end regime, for every list of blocks. Second, 41 rules for the left-end phase, each covering one round trip for every size, every list of units and every rest of the tape. Lean also shows (by the kernel for the first 35,911 steps, with native_decide for the first 7.7·106) that the run enters the right-end regime twice. Up to 3·107 steps, 5,449 of the 5,490 round trips that start at the left end are instances of these theorems. The other 41 are boundary cases, and none of them is proved. No halt in the first 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The right-end regime, for every list of blocks
claims.text: Write T a ks m for the tape (10)^(a+2) 1 (10)^(k_n+2) … 1 (10)^(k_1+2) (1101010)^(m+1) A>0, blank on both sides, with ks = [k_1, …, k_n] any list. One round trip of the head takes T (a+1) ks m to T a ks (m+1): the first counter loses one 10, the tail gains one 1101010, every block is crossed twice and comes back unchanged. Iterated: T (a+j) ks m reaches T a ks (m+j).

claims.title: The left-end phase: one round trip is a local rewrite
claims.text: Read the tape from a new leftmost cell (state A, blank to the left) as units (01)^b 0 0110, then (01)^a, then a frontier word w, then any rest S. If the first unit has b = x+2 and every other unit has b ≥ 2, one round trip takes the first unit to (01)^(x+1) 0 0110, leaves the other units alone, and rewrites (01)^(a+3) w as follows. 1 becomes (01)^(a+5) 0. 00101 becomes (01)^(a+7) 1. 001001 becomes (01)^(a+8). 0001 becomes (01)^(a+3) 00110011. 0000 becomes (01)^(a+3) 00110010. 001000 becomes (01)^(a+7) 00. With no unit in front, the same holds with one 01 fewer on the right. The cases a = 0, 1, 2 are separate rules. The proof uses tripGen: if the head turns at In and leaves 1 1 Out, the whole trip follows by induction on the list of units.
claims.where: lean/FrontierRules.lean (41 rules, generated by py/gen_frontier.py); tripGen and the 17 trip_tu*, trip_su* theorems, lean/Frontier.lean

claims.title: The cursor iterated
claims.text: Write F1 x bs c d for A> (01)^x 0 0110, then units bs, then the cursor (01)^c (10)^d 0110, then any rest. Write F2 for the same with the cursor (01)^c 0 (01)^d 0 0110. Then F1 (x+2) bs (c+2) (d+2) reaches F2 (x+1) bs (c+4) (d+1), and F2 (x+2) bs (c+2) (d+2) reaches F1 (x+1) bs (c+6) (d+1). Iterated, F1 (x+2j+1) bs (c+2) (d+2j+1) reaches F1 (x+1) bs (c+6j+2) (d+1).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 64,238 cells have been visited and 33,184 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.534). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.413).

claims.title: The run enters the regime after 35,911 steps
claims.text: After 35,911 steps from blank tape the configuration is T 108 [29, 4] 16 (evaluated by the kernel), so 108 round trips follow, to T 0 [29, 4] 124.

claims.title: And again after 7,677,126 steps, with 125 blocks
claims.text: After 7,677,126 steps the configuration is T 714 ks4 0, where ks4 is 8, then 3, 11 fifty-seven times, then 16, 123, 35, 123, 35, 123, 35, 123, 35, 235; so 714 round trips follow, to T 0 ks4 714. The bounded run is evaluated with native_decide.

claims.title: E never reads 1 with a 1 to its left (so far)
claims.text: The only halting entry is F reading a 1, and F is entered only from E>1 (write 1, move left): the machine halts exactly when 1 E>1 occurs. In the first 108 steps F is entered 687,974 times, always onto a 0, and in all but 38 of them the window around the head is 101[0]110.

claims.title: The regimes alternate
claims.text: The right-end regime runs at steps 2,889–7,790 (a = 13), 35,911–263,899 (a = 108), 7,677,126–21,453,756 (a = 714), 36,507,005–48,506,720 (a = 295) and from 250,823,121 (a = 7299, still running at 3·10<sup>8</sup>). In between, the head turns near the left end (the rewriting phase above). The tail survives these phases (m = 714, 717, 1012, 1015, …).

claims.title: Almost every trip from the left end is a proved rule
claims.text: Up to 3·107 steps there are 5,490 left-A records (the head on a new leftmost cell in state A). From 2,105 of them the trip is a whole-trip rule with no unit in front. From 2,509 it is a trip_tu*/trip_su* theorem. 835 lie inside a right-end regime. The remaining 41 are not covered: 32 have the first unit used up (b ≤ 1), 7 have a small frontier right after a unit (the rewrite starts a new unit), and 2 early ones have a small unit.

claims.title: No 1111 at the left-A records, and no halt from tapes without it
claims.text: At all 17,518 left-A records in the first 3·108 steps the tape has no factor 1111. Conversely, for every tape of at most 30 cells without 1111, the head started in A on its first cell (blank elsewhere) reaches the next left-A record without halting (387,559,437 tapes, at most 138 steps each). Every one-trip halt from a tape of at most 16 cells needs a 1111. The set of tapes without 1111 is not closed under a trip, though: about 4% of those trips create one.

claims.title: No halt in the first 8.29×10<sup>10</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 8.29×1010 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.04×1010 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 481 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Two things are missing. (i) Rules for the boundary trips: the first unit used up (b ≤ 1), the seven small frontiers right after a unit, units with b ≤ 1 outside the right-end regime, the word 00111 (never seen), and the switches into and out of the right-end regime. (ii) An invariant on the tapes that arise, strong enough that every trip is a proved rule or a boundary case. A sufficient conjecture: every left-A record has no factor 1111, and from every tape without 1111 the head reaches the next left-A record. Both halves are checked as described above, but neither is proved. The regime map (first counters 13, 108, 714, 295, 7299, …) comes from this rewriting acting on a list that keeps changing, and it looks open-ended.

claims.text: The same table as 1RB0RC_1LC0LD_1RA0LB_1LE0RA_1RD1LF_0LC--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine writes a list of numbers, each a run of 01s or 10s. In one regime, each sweep of the head takes one unit from the first number and adds a word at the right end. In the other, each sweep takes one unit from the first number and rewrites a few cells at the first place where the list is not regular. Both are proved in Lean for every size. What is not proved is the handful of special sweeps between them, and which tapes arise in the long run.

facts.text: Both proved one round trip at a time, for every size and every list of blocks.
Of the 5,490 trips from the left end in the first 3·10<sup>7</sup> steps, all but 41 are instances of the Lean theorems.
No halt in the C simulator.
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.04×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.heading: The one way to halt
html: The only halting entry is F reading a 1. F is entered only from E reading a 1 (E writes 1 and moves left), so the machine halts exactly when 1 E>1 occurs. In the first 108 steps E reads a 1 687,974 times; every time the cell to the left was a 0, and in all but 38 cases the cells around it read 101[0]110.

sections.heading: The right-end regime: one unit per trip
html: Stop the simulator whenever the head reaches a new cell at the right end in state A. At step 39,094 the tape reads
and 1,101 steps later

The head went left over the whole tape and back: going left it rewrites every block (10)^(k+2) 1 into 1 (10)^k 0 1 1 0 0, at the left end it adds one cell, and going right it restores each block as 1 (10)^(k+2), one cell further left. The net effect is that the first run of 10s is one shorter and the right end has one more word 1101010. Lean proves this for every first counter, every tail and every list of blocks in between (trip), by putting six generated pieces together with an induction on the list; trip_iter repeats it until the first counter is down to (10)^2.

sections.heading: Left-end phases: a local rewriting system
html: When the first counter is used up the right end stops growing, and for millions of steps the head turns near the left end instead. Stop the simulator whenever the head reaches a new leftmost cell in state A, and read the tape from the head. It is a list of units (01)^b 0 0110, then a run (01)^a, then a short frontier word, then a rest that the next trip will not touch. At step 22,147,896, for example, the tape starts

Here the units have 312 and 113, the run has 363, and the frontier word is 00101. In one round trip the head runs right over the units, turns at the frontier, runs back and adds a cell at the left. The first unit loses one 01 and (01)^a w is rewritten, nothing else:

• (01)^a 1 becomes (01)^(a+2) 0,
  • (01)^a 00101 becomes (01)^(a+4) 1,
  • (01)^a 001001 becomes (01)^(a+5),
  • (01)^a 0001 becomes (01)^a 00110011,
  • (01)^a 0000 becomes (01)^a 00110010,
  • (01)^a 001000 becomes (01)^(a+4) 00.

With no unit in front, each right side has one 01 fewer and nothing shrinks. After a maximal (01)^a the next cells are 1 or 00, so these six words, a new unit 00110, and 00111 (never seen) are all the cases. Lean proves each rule for every a, every list of units with b ≥ 2, and every rest (lean/Frontier.lean). The old picture of a pump and a cursor is this system at work. A cursor (01)^c (10)^d 0110 is the frontier 1 followed by (01)^(d-1) 0 0110. Two trips move c up by 6 and d down by 1, and when d is used up the words 0001 and 001001 turn the cursor into a new unit and start the next block as the cursor. With no unit in front, the same two trips are the pump.

Up to 3·107 steps, 41 trips from the left end are not covered. In 32 the first unit is used up and a later unit takes its place. In 7 a small frontier right after a unit starts a new unit. 2 are early trips with a small unit. Then the right-end regime starts again with a new first counter and a slightly changed list:

• steps 35,911 to 263,899: a = 108, 2 blocks;
  • steps 7,677,126 to 21,453,756: a = 714, 125 blocks (8, then 3, 11 fifty-seven times, then 16, 123, 35, 123, 35, 123, 35, 123, 35, 235), tail 0 to 714;
  • steps 36,507,005 to 48,506,720: a = 295, 123 blocks, tail 717 to 1012;
  • from step 250,823,121: a = 7299, 121 blocks, tail from 1015, still running at 3·108 steps.

The first two of these are entered in Lean (reach1, reach2) and run to their end with trip_iter. What is left is the boundary trips and an invariant on which tapes arise. A simple sufficient conjecture: no tape at a left-A record contains 1111, and from every tape without 1111 the next left-A record is reached. The second half holds for all tapes of at most 30 cells, and the first for the first 3·108 steps.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.534). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.413).
After 109 steps the tape spans 64,238 cells (39,116 left of the start, 11,124 right), with a density of 1s of 0.517.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0RC_1LC0LD_1RA0LB_1LE0RA_1RD1LF_0LC---: rename A→C, B→A, C→B, D→D, E→E, F→F; it is this table started in state B
  • 1RB0LC_1LA1RF_1LD0LE_1RE0RA_1LC0RD_0RE---: rename A→E, B→C, C→D, D→A, E→B, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror
  • 1RB0RD_1LC0RA_1LA0LB_1RE0LC_1LD1RF_0RB---: rename A→B, B→C, C→A, D→D, E→E, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state C, in a mirror
  • 1RB1LC_1LA0RE_0LD---_1RE0LF_1RF0RD_1LD0LB: rename A→D, B→E, C→F, D→B, E→A, F→C; it is this table started in state E

summary: Counter list with two regimes. Lean proves the right-end regime's round trip for every list of blocks, and the left-end phase as a local rewriting system: one round trip rewrites only the first unit and a short frontier word, for every size, every list of units and every rest (41 rules). The boundary trips between these and the map from one regime to the next are observed only.
family: counter list with a right-end regime and a left-end rewriting phase
